name: Cursed
label: Deathwish
lede: Chris Colohan finished with the Swarm and built Cursed across Montreal and Ontario, then made three albums loud enough that he got electrocuted on a video shoot. The last European tour ended with the passports and tour money stolen and one show left, in Amsterdam.

eras.title: After the Swarm
eras.text: Colohan had already sung in Left for Dead and the Swarm. Cursed was assembled from people he knew: him and Radwan Ghazi Moumneh in Montreal, Christian McMaster and Mike Maxymuik in Ontario, all aimed at playing hardcore slower and meaner.

years.h: The Swarm ends, and Chris Colohan starts Cursed
years.p: [[Chris Colohan|f1494c0a-331d-45dd-a51c-6c43d43ccc69]] takes McMaster on guitar and Maxymuik on drums, and adds Moumneh, who had played in the Quebec band Ire, on bass.
years.xp:
Wikipedia dates the founding to 2001, a year after the Swarm (also known as Knee Deep in the Dead) broke up. Colohan had sung in [[Left for Dead|cd47905f-3117-4bb2-9291-c258b240ef7d]], and Maxymuik had played with him in Ruination.

Colohan told Lambgoat in 2007 that the band started in winter 2001/02, with him and Moumneh in Montreal and McMaster and Maxymuik in Ontario. He and McMaster had been playing together since 1992, through Left for Dead, the Swarm and Cursed.

years.h: Cursed play their first show, at L'X in Montreal
years.p: The band's first show, February 15, 2002, was filmed. A self-released demo followed the same year, with the band still split between Montreal and Ontario.
years.xp: The date comes from the title of the footage posted on YouTube. Wikipedia lists the self-released demo for 2002 without a month.

years.h: Kurt Ballou produces the debut in Toronto
years.p: Cursed record their first album at Chemical Sound in Toronto, October 19 to 23, 2002, with [[Kurt Ballou|1e922902-2cb9-499f-aeb5-9a8c51dd0df0]] of [[Converge|fa31e7d4-a03a-4110-98fc-f8826e95ec25]] behind the board.
years.xp: Wikipedia gives the session dates and credits Ballou as producer. The album came out on Deathwish Inc., the label run by his Converge bandmate [[Jacob Bannon|d5c2a3e1-a52a-4af6-8e3f-aa2c4dc69af7]].

eras.title: Deathwish, then a real studio
eras.text: The debut on Deathwish earned the band a following. A second album at Chemical Sound with Ian Blurton on analog gear cleaned up the sound without softening it, and the bass spot changed hands once.

years.p: Twelve tracks, released February 25, 2003. It opens with Polygraph and runs close to seven minutes on Opposable Thumbs.

years.h: Moumneh picks up a guitar and Tom Piraino takes the bass
years.p: Tom "Dot Com" Piraino, who had played with McMaster in Funerary, comes in on bass. Moumneh becomes the second guitarist.

yt: Full set, Che Cafe, San Diego, Mar 20, 2004
years.h: "Hell Comes Home" on 7", then live in San Diego
years.p: Hex Records pressed a demo of the title track, backed with a cover of the Stooges' Search and Destroy, in 2,000 copies in several colors. A full set at the Che Cafe in San Diego, March 20, 2004, was filmed.
years.xp:
Hex Records' owner says he promised it would be a one-time pressing and never repressed. The title track was later re-recorded for II.

Colohan told the label's retrospective the song was about the blowback of exporting dominance and greed after 9/11. He also said it took a year of lining up their lives to be able to tour.

years.big: "Two is the first thing we're all pretty much totally happy with."
q: Two is the first thing we're all pretty much totally happy with.
years.h: II comes out on Goodfellow, mixed by Ian Blurton
years.p: Chris Colohan to Exclaim!, on the record released January 25, 2005. Thirty-four minutes, eleven tracks, including Model Home Invasion and Head of the Baptist.
years.xp:
Ian Blurton produced it at Chemical Sound, recording everything in analog. Colohan told Exclaim! it was easy to trust him "because he had a really good sense of what we were doing."

He also said the lyrics had moved from big-picture worldview toward cities and the individuals in them. Punknews, PopMatters and Lambgoat reviewed it, and Wikipedia says most reviews were positive.

years.h: Dan Dunham takes over on bass
years.p: Dunham, who also played in Shallow, North Dakota, keeps the bass spot until the band ends in 2008.
years.xp: Lambgoat has Dunham replacing Piraino in late 2004; Wikipedia and Exclaim! place the change in 2005.

eras.title: Volume machismo
eras.text: The live show was known for volume, and it cost Colohan at least one jolt on a video set. Compilations and reissues kept the catalog moving while the third album was written.

yt: Hell Comes Home live, London, Ontario, 2006
years.h: Colohan gets "wickedly electrocuted" on a video shoot
years.p: Exclaim! reported the band had cut back its amp stacks after incidents like this one. McMaster went from three heads and five cabinets to two of each.
years.xp:
In the same piece Colohan said of the old volume, "we were just blow places up," meaning clubs and PAs. Moumneh also runs two heads now.

Exclaim! gives no date for the shock itself, only that it happened during a video shoot.

years.p: A 2006 compilation of Cursed material that didn't make the albums.

years.h: Trash Art! repress I as a gatefold; Blackout at Sunrise gets a picture disc
years.p: The debut came back on 180-gram vinyl in a gatefold sleeve. The band also issued the Blackout at Sunrise picture-disc EP.

eras.title: Three, then Amsterdam
eras.text: The third album was the band's biggest release. The European tour behind it ended in Amsterdam, and the band never played again.

years.cap: Cursed's four members in a van, 2008
yt: Studio footage from the III sessions, Jan 2008
years.h: III: Architects of Troubled Sleep closes the trilogy
years.p: Eleven tracks from Architects of Troubled Sleep to Gutters. Goodfellow released it in North America, Howling Bull in Japan and Reflections in Europe.
years.xp:
Recorded at Hallamusic in Toronto, mixed by Donny Cooper and mastered by Alan Douches. Colohan told Lambgoat the band mixed it until they were happy, cleaner than any earlier recording but with deep guitar loudness.

The cover is by [[Baroness|eeb41a1e-4326-4d04-8c47-0f564ceecd68]] frontman John Baizley. Deathwish later pressed it on vinyl in Silver, White/Black mix and Clear with Brown splatter, and called it the band's hardest-hitting album.

years.h: A sold-out Lee's Palace, after six weekends of DIY shows
years.p: Before the album came out, Cursed played six weekends of Southern Ontario DIY shows. The Toronto release show at Lee's Palace, with 50Watthead, Career Suicide and Living Darkness, sold out.

years.big: "A bullet in the head, the end of the line."
q: A bullet in the head, the end of the line.
years.h: Robbed in Germany, finished in Amsterdam
years.p: On May 22, 2008, Colohan wrote that the band had lost passports, money and tour funds to a robbery in Germany. Cursed played a last show at Bitterzoet in Amsterdam.
years.xp:
Colohan called it "a sudden and totally fucked up way for it to end." The plan for the last show, he wrote: "play the show, badly, and go our ways."

He said the tour, apart from the last chaotic shows, had been their best, and that all outstanding plans were off. Afterward he hitched a ride to Prague.

eras.title: What came next
eras.text: Colohan kept the catalog in print and kept playing. The others ended up in Montreal's experimental scene and other bands.

years.h: Colohan puts Cursed's last UK radio session on 7"
years.p: The Last Session comes out on High Anxiety, his own vinyl-only label.

years.h: Four ex-Cursed members, four new places to land
years.p: Colohan plays in [[Burning Love|47ad0632-61da-455b-9674-a159b3eea43e]] and Mature Situations. Maxymuik joins Quest for Fire and tours with Pink Mountaintops. Dunham plays in Crux of Aux, Skull and Limitoids.
years.xp: Moumneh co-opened Hotel2Tango in Montreal with people from Godspeed You! Black Emperor and Constellation Records, and continues the performance project Jerusalem in My Heart.

years.h: Colohan forms SECT with Fall Out Boy's Andy Hurley
years.p: Hurley plays drums, with James Chang and Scott Crouse on guitar and Ian Edwards on bass.

years.h: Deathwish makes a 90-minute cassette of Cursed
years.p: A Young Person's Guide to Cursed puts 30 tracks from all three albums on a handmade 8-track tape. The label called Cursed a very important band to Deathwish.
